title: Personal Checking: Interest-Bearing Tiers and Their APY Ladders
content:
Three Personal Checking tiers pay interest and three do not. Each interest-bearing tier publishes a ladder of balance bands: a band starts at its floor, stated in USD, and carries an annual percentage yield stated in percent. A day's whole end-of-day balance earns the APY of the highest floor it reaches.

## Which tiers pay interest

| Tier | Pays interest |
|---|---|
| Access Checking | no |
| Student Checking | no |
| Everyday Checking | no |
| Interest Checking | yes |
| Premier Checking | yes |
| Private Client Checking | yes |

Access, Student and Everyday Checking each carry a single band from 0.00 USD at an APY of 0.00 percent.

## Ladders of the interest-bearing tiers

**Interest Checking**

| Band floor (USD) | APY (percent) |
|---|---|
| 0.00 | 0.01 |
| 10000.00 | 0.02 |
| 25000.00 | 0.05 |
| 100000.00 | 0.10 |

**Premier Checking**

| Band floor (USD) | APY (percent) |
|---|---|
| 0.00 | 0.02 |
| 10000.00 | 0.05 |
| 25000.00 | 0.10 |
| 100000.00 | 0.15 |

**Private Client Checking**

| Band floor (USD) | APY (percent) |
|---|---|
| 0.00 | 0.05 |
| 25000.00 | 0.15 |
| 100000.00 | 0.25 |
| 250000.00 | 0.35 |

## Reading a band (hypothetical balances)

- A Premier Checking day ending at 24999.99 USD reaches the 10000.00 floor but not the 25000.00 floor, so the whole balance takes 0.05 percent.
- A Private Client Checking day ending at exactly 250000.00 USD reaches the top floor, so the whole balance takes 0.35 percent.
